notes: Moov webhook body confirmation (2026-10-31, security audit 2026-10-29): Moov signs timestamp|nonce|webhookID, not the body, so one set of signed headers could be resent for five minutes with any body and set a transfer's status, a Collection V2 obligation's settlement or an account's onboarding status. The accepted bytes: providers/webhooks.mjs keys the Moov receipt on the signed X-Webhook-ID only (never the body eventID) and, before any apply, reads the transfer, account or bank account the body names back from Moov through the added providers/moov-webhook-confirm.mjs (GET only, the calls and credentials the existing code already uses: resolveBillingMoovContext, production keys only on the production runtime) and applies only what Moov returned; a resource Moov does not know is not applied, a Moov outage rolls the receipt back and answers 503 so Moov delivers again. tenant-collection-v2-settlement.mjs matches the ' · moov:<transfer id>' notes token exactly instead of notes LIKE '%id%'. No SQL; no money movement; no other member changes. webhooks.mjs live_sha256 f7353ee1 and tenant-collection-v2-settlement.mjs live_sha256 075d96d0 are the bytes the third full-package production rebuild put live (ops/deployment-guard/lambda-rebuild-plan.json, production run 39669873076 of main 008af40e2, CodeSha256 pNCewAaF...); neither file changed on main since, and no overlay of either has been planned or applied since. webhooks.mjs chains to the manifest that planned f7353ee1 (previous_manifest). moov-webhook-confirm.mjs is new, so it has no live bytes; webhooks.mjs imports it at load, so it is ordered just before webhooks.mjs.
